name: Trump Hotel, Doonbeg Ireland
positioning: Trump International Golf Links & Hotel Ireland, Doonbeg: a links golf resort on Doughmore Bay in west County Clare, with suites that have kitchens and the White Horses Spa
best_for: Golfers who want a links course set in the dunes along Doughmore Bay
Families and groups who want suites with kitchens and activities like horse riding, falconry and a kids' clubhouse

facts.text: The resort sits on a remote bay in west County Clare.
The building looks like a nineteenth-century seaside manor but was built in 2006.
The golf course has been transformed by Dr. Martin Hawtree.
Suites have one to four bedrooms, with high ceilings, gas fireplaces and kitchens.
Guest rooms are appointed with curated furnishings, art and antiques.
White Horses Spa is inspired by 5,000 years of Irish history and mystery.
The spa uses Repêchage, a skincare brand founded on sustainably harvested seaweed.
The spa menu includes deep tissue massages for golfers seeking post-round recovery.
Guests can go surfing at Doughmore Beach.
Nearby County Clare excursions include Doolin Cave, Aillwee Cave and Bunratty Castle.
Diversions for non-golfers include dolphin watching and hiking the nearby cliffs.
The hotel received the Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star Hotel Award in 2025.

highlights.text: The 18-hole championship links course spans 1.5 miles of crescent-shaped beach and century-old sand dunes along Doughmore Bay.
The spa has signature copper baths, offered as part of a curated collection of seaweed bathing rituals.
As early as 1892, officers of the Scottish Black Watch Regiment considered Doonbeg an ideal setting for links golf.
Horse riding is offered as a beach ride or a country adventure, and guests can also try falconry and archery.
Families can use the Junior Clubhouse, which has a soft playroom.

considerations.text: The golf course is closed from January 4 to February 4, 2027.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires significant travel time.
WhataHotel notes outdoor activities depend on the weather.
